findings.title: include_website_name missing '?' so website_name leaks for restricted TL0 users
findings.body: The method is named `include_website_name` without the trailing `?`, so ActiveModel::Serializers never calls it as a filter. `website_name` is also not listed in `untrusted_attributes`. As a result, `website_name` is serialized even when `website` is hidden by `restrict_user_fields?`, for example a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor. This exposes the hidden website and partly defeats the anti-spam restriction. The method should be renamed to `include_website_name?` and apply the same restriction check, or `website_name` should be added to `untrusted_attributes`.

findings.title: Subdomain check uses naive suffix matching on short hosts
findings.body: The fallback branch treats any website host that is a dot-suffix of the forum host as the 'same' site. If the website host is a public suffix such as `co.uk` and the forum is `forum.example.co.uk`, the check matches and the full path is shown. The same-length branch has a similar flaw: hosts like `a.co.uk` and `b.co.uk` are treated as the same domain because they share the `co.uk` suffix. The domain comparison is unreliable for multi-part TLDs.

findings.title: No test for TL0/anonymous hiding website_name or for sibling subdomains
findings.body: The TL0 context's `untrusted_attributes` list was not extended with `website_name`, so the leak of `website_name` for restricted users is not caught by the specs. The `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` branch of `website_name` is also untested.
